what_happened: Confirmed directly in orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's own header comments that its collision comparison set already excludes any dependencies[]-edge-connected pair in either direction (A1 note) -- this means the dispatch's EDGE-PROPOSING STEP requires no new admission logic at all: add the edge via update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add, then re-probe the real script. Saves the implementation phase from having to discover or re-derive this mechanism empirically.

Research-flagged file_scope gap (commands/orchestrate.md, the only queue-check call site, absent from the declared four-entry file_scope) was resolved mechanically at plan time rather than mid-implementation: listing every touched file in the phases' 'Files to modify' blocks makes plan-file-scope-harvest.sh widen file_scope from 4 to 10 entries at plan postflight, the one moment --file-scope-add is admissible. Verified by running the harvester over the finished plan (10/10 paths harvested).

The EDGE-PROPOSING STEP's 'PROPOSE the serializing edge via update-task-status.sh --depends-on-add' admits two readings: emit the command, or perform the write (the latter being the only way the acceptance criterion's re-probe can show admit). Resolved in-plan as Decision 2 rather than escalated to the user: propose-only by default (conclusion time is the wrong moment to mutate state.json dependency edges unasked), with an opt-in --write-edges flag that writes then re-probes, and the acceptance demonstration run under --write-edges against a scratch tree.

Proved the selection doctrine's width-vs-chain nuance is vacuous within a ready-only candidate pool: a ready task's dependencies[] entries can never themselves be ready-pool members, since a predecessor must be status=completed (terminal, hence excluded from readiness). Simplified select_candidates() accordingly and documented the proof inline instead of implementing dead code.

Discovered update-task-status.sh's map_status() has no operation:target_status combination that resolves to state.json status 'not_started' -- so --depends-on-add cannot be issued as a no-op status call against a task still in its initial status. The edge-proposing step detects this (resolve_noop_token() returns 1) and falls back to a loud propose-only rendering rather than guessing or failing silently. Confirmed live: tasks 385/464 collide on file_scope in the real specs/state.json, and task 464 is 'not_started', exercising this exact branch.

Live-testing Mode A against the real specs/state.json (via a temporary gitignored .claude/scripts/ copy, removed after each test, with before/after diffs confirming no mutation) surfaced a genuine, previously-unknown file_scope collision between tasks 385 and 464 that orchestrate-batch-admit.sh correctly detected and the edge-proposing step correctly rendered as an ordered sequence. Real end-to-end validation, not just a synthetic fixture.

The fixture suite's own construction process (deliberately building a scratch-tree reproduction of the real admission chain) caught two genuine implementation/test-design gaps before they shipped: (1) update-task-status.sh's --depends-on-add no-op path needs state-write.sh and generate-todo.sh in the scratch dependency copy list, which the plan's own starting-hypothesis copy list did not enumerate; (2) orchestrate-batch-admit.sh exempts a research/plan-routed absent-file_scope candidate from the blocking in_batch defer branch unconditionally, which the fixture (d) design had to account for by routing its candidates to planned/implement instead of not_started. Both were confirmed by reading the real admission script's own source rather than guessing.

Gate 3 (doc-lint) initially failed for three real, mechanical findings: index-entries.json line_count drift for conclusion-stage.md, batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, and orchestrate-batch-results-template.md (the three markdown files this phase edited). Resolved by running the sanctioned bash .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write remedy the lint itself names. A fourth, EXPECTED finding remains after that fix: 'deployed script content drift' for scripts/tests/suite-cost-hints.txt, purely because .claude/ has not been redeployed since Phase 4's edit to that already-deployed file -- a pending-deploy state, not a defect, and out of scope for this dispatch to resolve independently (regeneration is manual-only per this repo's own convention; the batch-level stage's own redeploy checkpoint is the correct place for it to clear).
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
